Run one SAS step in a session

Source: R/script.R
sas_step_verbs.Rd

The verbs of a script written by sas_script(). Each takes a session from sas_session(), runs one step in it as sas_run() does (the log, the listing, WORK and the macro variables of the session change), and returns the session invisibly, so the calls can be chained with |>.

Usage

sas_data_step(session, data, fn, sas, line = 1L, level = NULL)

sas_proc_sort(session, options = "", ..., line = 1L)

sas_proc_means(session, options = "", ..., line = 1L)

sas_proc_sql(session, sql, options = "", line = 1L)

sas_proc(session, sas, line = 1L)

sas_options(session, options, line = 1L)

sas_title(session, title = "", n = 1L, line = 1L)

sas_global(session, sas, line = 1L)

sas_deferred(session, sas, line = 1L)

Arguments

session

A session from sas_session().

data

The output data sets of the DATA step (for the reader; the SAS text names them).

fn

A function of work whose body is the code of the step.

sas

SAS text of the step.

line

The SAS line the step starts on (line numbers in the log).

level

NULL (the level of the translation) or "L3" (the step ran row by row).

options

Options of the PROC (or OPTIONS) statement as SAS text.

...

Statements of the PROC step: name = "text".

sql

SQL statements, each ending with a semicolon.

title

The text of a TITLE statement (quoted SAS strings).

n

The title line (TITLEn).

Value

The session, invisibly.

Details

  • sas_data_step() runs the R code of fn (the code sasonr generated for the DATA step sas) in place of the translation of sas; the SAS text gives the variable attributes of the output data sets and the log. When vectorised code meets a data error the step is run again row by row from its SAS text, as in sas_run().

  • sas_proc_sort(), sas_proc_means(): the options of the PROC statement and one argument per statement (by = "usubjid", output = "out=m mean="), as the program wrote them.

  • sas_proc_sql(): the SQL statements of a PROC SQL step.

  • sas_proc(): any PROC step as SAS text.

  • sas_options(), sas_title(), sas_global(): global statements.

  • sas_deferred(): SAS text with macro code, run through the macro processor (code that depends on values known only at run time).

Examples

s <- sas_session(work = list(a = data.frame(x = c(2, 1, 3))))
s |> sas_proc_sort("data=a out=b", by = "descending x")
s |> sas_proc_means("data=b noprint", var = "x", output = "out=m mean=xm")
sas_work(s)$m
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   `_type_` `_freq_`    xm
#>      <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1        0        3     2
